Both are already linked to 131 common concepts, including coordination, education and gender, which suggests the methods and data needed to connect them already exist. We propose a study that uses coordination as a bridge: first, review how execution and reliance are each currently treated through coordination; second, design an approach that combines them and test it on established benchmarks from both lines of work; third, measure whether the combination improves on each topic studied alone. We expect the work to clarify where the two literatures overlap and to open a new line of research between them.

Both are already linked to 136 common concepts, including monte carlo method, open source software and quality control, which suggests the methods and data needed to connect them already exist. We propose a study that uses monte carlo method as a bridge: first, review how python and usability are each currently treated through monte carlo method; second, design an approach that combines them and test it on established benchmarks from both lines of work; third, measure whether the combination improves on each topic studied alone. We expect the work to clarify where the two literatures overlap and to open a new line of research between them.
